title: Descent of a bounded principal-open cover
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c,d\in\mathbf N$, and $f_i\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $R_0\subseteq R$ be a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subring [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $f_{0,i}\in R_0[x]$ mapping to $f_i$. Write $S_0=R_0[x]/(f_0)$ and $S=R[x]/(f)$. Let $\iota$ be any indexing set and $G_j\in R_0[x]$ for $j\in\iota$. Assume their images avoid every prime of $S$ for at least one $j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and every nonzero fibre of $R_0\to(S_0)_{\bar G_j}$ has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then there exist a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subring $R_1\subseteq R$ and equations $f_{1,i}\in R_1[x]$ mapping to $f_i$, such that for each prime $p_1\subset R_1$ whose fibre of $S_1=R_1[x]/(f_1)$ is nonzero, $\iota$ is inhabited and this fibre has dimension at most $d$. In particular, for an empty indexing set $S_1$ is zero. No complete-intersection hypothesis and no lower dimension bound occur in this statement.

proof.text: The avoidance hypothesis means the principal opens cover Spec S. Quasi-compactness selects finitely many indices J. The unit-ideal criterion gives 1 = ∑ h̄ⱼ ḡⱼ in S. Lift h̄ⱼ to polynomials hⱼ over R. The difference 1-∑ hⱼ map(Gⱼ) lies in the ideal generated by the finite family f, so is ∑ aᵢfᵢ. If Spec S is empty use J empty and 1=∑ aᵢfᵢ.

Choose a finite generating set for R₀ over ℤ. Form R₁ by adjoining its images and the finitely many coefficients of f, the selected Gⱼ, hⱼ and aᵢ. Finiteness of these sets makes R₁ finite type over ℤ and it contains R₀. Lift each polynomial coefficientwise to R₁. Injectivity of R₁ → R proves the lifted polynomial identity, which makes the lifted gⱼ generate 1 in S₁. This constructs the coefficient ring rather than choosing arbitrary data in a definition.

Contract p₁ to p₀ in R₀. Polynomial and quotient base change together with localization base change identify the localized p₁-fibre as scalar extension of the localized p₀-fibre along κ(p₀) → κ(p₁). A nonzero new fibre implies a nonzero old one, since scalar extension of the zero ring is zero. The old fibre is finite type over κ(p₀). The global field-extension dimension theorem preserves its dimension, so each nonzero localized new fibre has dimension ≤ d.

The unit identity shows the corresponding principal opens cover every p₁-fibre. At any fibre point choose a selected open containing it; the localization spectrum is that open, and local dimension is unchanged there. Its local dimension is ≤ its global dimension ≤ d. The supremum of local dimensions bounds the entire fibre by d. If the fibre is nonzero it has a prime, whose selected open gives an index in ι. With an empty cover the descended unit identity instead makes S₁ zero.
